title: Knowing Isn't Understanding: Can You Explain It in Your Own Words?
summary:
A student spends three hours studying a chapter.
They memorize definitions, practise model answers, and score well in an examination.
A few months later, someone asks:
“Can you explain this in your own words?”
Suddenly, the answer becomes difficult.
Why?
The student may remember the information. But recognizing an answer and reconstructing it independently are two different skills.
Perhaps this explains a familiar experience many of us have had:
“I know this. So why can't I explain it?”

title: What Should Beginners Learn First in 2026: Fundamentals or AI Tools? 🤔
summary:
A beginner asked me something last week that I haven't stopped thinking about.
"Should I learn JavaScript properly first, or just start building with AI?"
I didn't have a clean answer.

Because both sides make sense.
If you don't understand what the code does, you can't tell when AI gets it wrong.
And AI gets things wrong in quiet ways. The code runs. The tests pass. But the logic is off, or there's a security hole, or it breaks the moment real users show up.
Someone has to notice that.
